newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on commercial demand, China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on commercial demand, China.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed higher on commercial buying and on a rumor China was seeking up to 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for October shipment, traders said.
"There are still rumors of China buying as much as 100,000 tonnes of meal for October," a trader said.
Gains in soymeal were trimmed and pressure on soyoil came from a drop in soybean futures tied to fund selling and to bearish weather factors.
Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for normal to above normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation in the U.S. Midwest from October 1 through October 5.
Funds sold at least 1,600 lots of soyoil with LIT America the chief seller of 1,100 December, the traders said.
In soymeal, Continental Grain bought 500 December, Refco Inc bought 600 December and LIT America bought 500 lots of December, they said.
Soymeal closed $1.30 per ton higher to $2.00 lower, with October up $1.30 at $264.50. Soyoil was 0.05 to 0.35 cent per lb lower, with October down 0.35 at 24.56.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, up from 25,028 Wednesday, according to the CBOT. Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, up from 16,994 Wednesday.
